title: The Orchard of the Lower Danube
premise: Ines Amberdale, a pearl diver's son indentured to the Varga Trading Company on the lower Danube, has spent nine years making himself unremarkable—until imperial troops requisition the river town and seize the company ledger bearing every bonded worker's name. When Ines learns his own page marks him for conscription aboard a naval galley, he strikes a bargain: finish restoring the workshop's flood-damaged pearl stock before the requisition ship sails on the morning tide, and his name will be struck from the ledger. Racing floods, suspicion, and his growing love for Mira, the quartermaster's daughter who keeps the ledger's duplicate, Ines must choose between erasing himself forever and signing his name to something worth being seen for. He finishes the work, but at dawn he refuses the bargain—claiming his name publicly—and sails not as cargo but as a free man of the orchard town, with Mira beside him.
about_author: Jude Villalobos is the pen name of a former river-cargo clerk who spent three years cataloguing shipping ledgers in Balkan port towns before turning to fiction. Their work explores how ordinary laborers survive the collisions of empire, trade, and memory.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Hands
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Nine years after his father drowned diving for pearls, Ines works silently in the Varga workshop, mending nets and sorting shells, determined to remain invisible among the indentured workers. Emotional beat: quiet resignation masking an old grief.

chapters.title: Ledger Lines
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. The quartermaster's daughter copies names into the company ledger and notices Ines's page—his father's debt transferred to his own name at age eleven. She watches him work without revealing what she knows. Emotional beat: curiosity kindling into sympathy.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Water
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Imperial gunboats appear downriver; rumor spreads that the army will requisition the town, its stores, and its people. The workshop master orders double shifts. Emotional beat: dread seeping into routine.

chapters.title: The Orchard Above the Docks
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Ines and Mira meet by chance in the abandoned orchard above the wharf, both seeking escape from the tightening town. They speak honestly for the first time. Emotional beat: tentative connection across class lines.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Soldiers occupy the town; officers seal the countinghouse and confiscate the ledger with every bonded worker's name inside. The workshop master is detained for questioning. Emotional beat: the ground giving way beneath everything certain.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. Mira learns her father kept a duplicate ledger hidden in the orchard storehouse—and that Ines's page bears a red mark: conscription to the naval galleys when the ship sails. Emotional beat: horror at complicity in her father's system.

chapters.title: A Bargain Struck in Shell-Light
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Through Mira, Ines negotiates with the occupying paymaster: restore the flood-soaked pearl stock to saleable condition before the morning tide, and his name is struck from the rolls. Emotional beat: desperate hope laced with distrust.

chapters.title: Nine Days of Salt
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The restoration begins—boiling, drying, grading thousands of waterlogged pearls alone in the sealed workshop while soldiers patrol outside. His hands remember his father's teaching. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into craft.

chapters.title: The Quartermaster's House
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. Mira confronts her father about the debt that bound Ines; he defends it as arithmetic, not cruelty. She steals the duplicate ledger's key. Emotional beat: loyalty fracturing along moral lines.

chapters.title: Flood Season
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Spring melt swells the Danube; water breaches the warehouse cellar where half the restored stock is stored. Ines works through the night hauling crates upward as soldiers refuse to help a 'company property.' Emotional beat: isolation sharpened into defiance.

chapters.title: Names Are Not Cargo
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. Mira discovers other red-marked pages—twelve workers slated for the galleys, not just Ines. Her private rescue plan becomes a larger question she cannot answer alone. Emotional beat: guilt expanding into responsibility.

chapters.title: The Orchard at Night
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Ines and Mira meet again in the orchard; she confesses the twelve names, he rages that she hid it, then understands her fear. They plan together. Emotional beat: conflict deepening into partnership and love.

chapters.title: An Officer's Patience
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Captain Dreven, the requisition officer, grows suspicious of the workshop's night activity and begins auditing the pearl count daily, threatening the deadline. Emotional beat: the walls closing in.

chapters.title: Grading by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. With four days left, Ines trains two fellow indentured workers in secret to speed the work, breaking his own rule of never trusting anyone. Emotional beat: invisibility deliberately surrendered.

chapters.title: The Duplicate
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. Mira copies the twelve red-marked pages and hides them in the orchard wall, but her father catches her returning and realizes what she knows. Emotional beat: terror balanced by resolve.

chapters.title: What the Master Knew
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Released from detention, the old workshop master reveals that Ines's father died not in accident but saving the company's stock during the last flood—a debt the ledger never recorded. Emotional beat: rage and revaluation of his whole life.

chapters.title: The Count Comes Up Short
chapters.summary: Dreven's POV (brief) shifting to Ines's. A final audit finds pearls missing—stolen by a soldier, but Ines is blamed. The bargain hangs by a thread hours before the tide. Emotional beat: betrayal of every rule he obeyed.

chapters.title: Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The ship's bells ring; the work is finished, but Dreven reneges, ordering Ines aboard with the others. On the dock, Mira steps forward with the duplicate ledger and accuses her father publicly. Emotional beat: climax—the choice between safety and truth made in front of everyone.

chapters.title: Twelve Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. Mira reads the twelve names to the assembled town and officers; the workers step forward one by one, claiming themselves. Dreven, facing mutiny among his own conscripts, relents under the town's united gaze. Emotional beat: collective courage breaking solitary fear.

chapters.title: The Last Page
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines takes the pen and writes his own name—not to be erased, but signed to a new register Mira has drawn up: a free cooperative of the orchard workers. Emotional beat: identity claimed rather than hidden.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The requisition ship sails empty of the town's people; Ines dives into the flooded shallows where his father died and surfaces with the season's first pearl, given to no ledger. Emotional beat: mourning finally finding peace.

chapters.title: Blossom Over the Danube
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Weeks later, the orchard blooms above a rebuilt workshop; Ines and Mira hang the old ledger's final page on the wall as a memorial to every name once owned. Emotional beat: belonging earned, love chosen, memory honored.
